text:
Jen Park: Quick design check — I sketched two validation patterns for Settings > Integrations. Option A: inline error under each field + subtle red asterisk for required. Option B: minimal inline, then a submit-time toast with error summary that links to fields. Which should we standardize on? Concerns: mobile vertical space, screen reader announcements, and clarity for quick fixes. Maria Gomez: leaning strongly toward inline. Users fix faster if error is next to the input. Toasts are easy to miss on mobile or when keyboard open. :+1: Tariq Hassan: Agree with Maria. Also: how do we handle required markers? Asterisks are compact but often meaningless to AT. Maybe use visible "Required" helper text for screen readers? Patrick Li: For dense admin forms I get wanting to reduce visual noise, so toast + linked summary can work, but we'd need anchors and focus management to move to first error. Otherwise accessibility suffers. Jen Park: Good point — if we went toast we must shift focus to the first errored field and announce the count. Example pattern: after submit, focus -> #field-1 and SR live region: "2 errors found — moved to first error". Thoughts on copy? Maria Gomez: Prefer explicit inline copy: e.g., "Email is required" vs just red outline + asterisk. Also prefer the required indicator to be visible text on small viewports (e.g., "Email · Required") so it reads naturally for screen readers. Tariq Hassan: Quick ARIA snippet we can reuse: ```
Email is required
``` That gives both visual cue and SR announcement. Patrick Li: For destructive actions (delete integration) we also need to decide typed-confirm vs checkbox confirm vs modal with warning. My vote: typed-confirm for persistent resources with billing implications, otherwise confirm modal with clear CTA. Jen Park: Agreed — typed confirm only for high-risk. For others, we can use a modal with primary/destructive button states + undo toast where possible. Also need to unify microcopy: typed confirm should be short: "Type DELETE to confirm removing this integration." Maria Gomez: Nit: make the typed-confirm input auto-focus and use monospace to differentiate user input. Add aria-describedby for hint that it's case sensitive (or explicitly say it's not). ARIA (design-bot): Accessibility checklist reminder: 1) focus management to first error, 2) role=alert for inline errors, 3) keyboard-only flow tested, 4) mobile viewport checks, 5) color contrast for error text >= 4.5:1. Tariq Hassan: One more UX nit — required asterisk color should not be solely red (contrast), maybe use alpha plus word "Required" on hover for dense screens. Patrick Li: Implementation note for runtime: backend validation returns field keys + messages; front-end will map to field IDs. If we standardize on inline, we can reuse the same JSON shape but render toast fallback in constrained screens. Jen Park: Proposed outcome: default to inline errors + visible "Required" label on mobile and for SR; allow an optional submit-summary toast that also directs focus to first error (for dense forms). Typed-confirm for high-risk destructive actions only. I'll update the spec and mockups. Anyone object? Maria Gomez: No objections. Please include copy examples and the ARIA snippet in the spec. Patrick Li: Fine with me. Can we add a small acceptance test: keyboard-only reproduction + screen reader read-through? Tariq Hassan: I'll add accessibility test cases to the ticket. Jen Park: Thanks all — I'll post updated Figma screens and the spec in the doc. :rocket: Maria Gomez: :thumbsup: ARIA (design-bot): Filing accessibility follow-up: #A11Y-4572 Patrick Li: Also leaving a tiny CSS suggestion in the doc: `.error-hint { font-weight: 600; }` — keeps emphasis without loud color. Jen Park: Noted, will include. End of thread.
